title: Logic App Run Failures

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.2.38 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.2.38 search returns zero rows.

description: Integration workflows power automation; failed runs leave tickets, data, and approvals stuck.
value: Detecting logic app run failures early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Enable Logic App workflow diagnostics. Ingest run status and error codes. Alert on any failed production workflow or retry exhaustion. Replay failed runs from operations team process.
visualization: Table (workflow, error), Timeline (failures), Single value (failed runs / hour).
knownFalsePositives: This pattern can surge during change windows, in sandboxes, and when a platform is in maintenance, so we line alerts up with the calendar and take a second look before we call it an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=azure`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` with the modular input for `mscs:azure:diagnostics`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.2.58.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable Logic App workflow diagnostics. Ingest run status and error codes. Alert on any failed production workflow or retry exhaustion. Replay failed runs from operations team process.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:diagnostics" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:diagnostics" resourceType="Microsoft.Logic/workflows" status_s="Failed"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.38_logic_app_run_failures_38"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `mscs:azure:diagnostics` in `index=azure` to detect logic app run failures. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_38_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Table (workflow, error), Timeline (failures), Single value (failed runs / hour)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of logic app run failures so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
